# How this script works

Every figure is drawn from a small **summary table** (counts, percentages, means), never
from client-level records. The tables in the `data` chunk are stand-ins: Figure 1 uses the
SHAREABLE figures already in the Section 5 draft; the rest are mock values with the right
shape. To use real results, replace each stand-in tibble with a `read_csv()` of the matching
SHAREABLE export and rename its columns to the ones listed above each plotting function.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)
```

```{r config}
SUPPRESS_N <- params$suppress_n
FIG_WIDTH  <- params$fig_width
OUT_DIR    <- params$output_dir
dir.create(OUT_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

PAL <- c(ink = "#22303C", grey = "#9AA5B1", light = "#E4E7EB",
         accent = "#0B6E75", warm = "#D1603D")
PAL_QUAL <- c("#0B6E75", "#D1603D", "#E3A72F", "#5B5F97", "#7FB069", "#9AA5B1", "#22303C")
SUPPR_LABEL  <- "Suppr."
MOCK_CAPTION <- "MOCK DATA: placeholder values for layout only."
TITLE_WIDTH  <- 62   # characters per title line at FIG_WIDTH
```

```{r helpers}
theme_report <- function(base_size = 10) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      text = element_text(colour = PAL[["ink"]]),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = rel(1.15)),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = PAL[["grey"]], margin = margin(b = 8)),
      plot.caption = element_text(colour = PAL[["grey"]], hjust = 0, size = rel(0.8)),
      plot.caption.position = "plot",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      axis.title = element_text(size = rel(0.9)),
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.justification = "left",
      legend.title = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
      strip.placement = "outside"
    )
}

# A row is suppressed when its n is below the threshold or its value is already blank
# (SHAREABLE exports blank suppressed cells, including complementary suppression).
is_suppressed <- function(n, value, threshold = SUPPRESS_N) {
  is.na(value) | (!is.na(n) & n < threshold)
}

finding <- function(text) str_wrap(text, TITLE_WIDTH)   # wrap long finding-style titles

save_fig <- function(plot, name, height, width = FIG_WIDTH) {
  ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0(name, ".png")), plot,
         width = width, height = height, dpi = params$dpi, bg = "white")
  plot
}
```

# Figure 1. Extended dumbbell: unadjusted vs. adjusted satisfaction

Needs: `dimension`, `level`, `n`, `unadjusted`, `adjusted` (percentages).

```{r fig1-dumbbell}
plot_dumbbell <- function(df, ref_value) {
  df <- df |>
    filter(!is_suppressed(n, adjusted), !is.na(unadjusted)) |>
    mutate(gap = adjusted - unadjusted,
           level = fct_reorder(level, gap),
           dimension = fct_inorder(dimension))
  pts <- df |>
    pivot_longer(c(unadjusted, adjusted), names_to = "estimate", values_to = "pct") |>
    mutate(estimate = fct_inorder(str_to_sentence(estimate)))

  ggplot(df, aes(y = level)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = ref_value, colour = PAL[["grey"]], linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_segment(aes(x = unadjusted, xend = adjusted, yend = level),
                 colour = PAL[["light"]], linewidth = 3.5, lineend = "round") +
    geom_point(data = pts, aes(x = pct, colour = estimate), size = 3.2) +
    geom_text(aes(x = (unadjusted + adjusted) / 2, label = sprintf("%+.1f", gap)),
              vjust = -1, size = 2.6, colour = PAL[["ink"]]) +
    facet_grid(dimension ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = unname(PAL[c("warm", "accent")])) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(scale = 1)) +
    scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.6, 0.9))) +
    labs(x = "Reported high satisfaction", y = NULL) +
    theme_report() +
    theme(strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, vjust = 1))
}

fig1 <- plot_dumbbell(sat_adjusted, SAT_OVERALL) +
  labs(title = finding(paste("Satisfaction gaps between rounds and groups narrowed after adjustment;",
                             "the gap by discharge reason widened")),
       subtitle = "Percentage-point change from unadjusted to adjusted rate shown above each bar",
       caption = paste0("Dashed line: overall rate (", SAT_OVERALL,
                        "%). Groups under ", SUPPRESS_N, " not shown."))
save_fig(fig1, "fig1_satisfaction_dumbbell", height = 5.2)
```

# Figure 2. Diverging stacked bars: full satisfaction scale

Needs: `group`, `n`, `response` (ordered factor, low to high, odd number of levels), `pct`.

```{r fig2-likert}
plot_likert <- function(df) {
  k   <- nlevels(df$response)
  mid <- (k + 1) / 2
  df <- df |>
    filter(!is_suppressed(n, pct)) |>
    group_by(group) |>
    arrange(response, .by_group = TRUE) |>
    mutate(idx    = as.integer(response),
           offset = sum(pct[idx < mid]) + sum(pct[idx == mid]) / 2,
           xmax   = cumsum(pct) - offset,
           xmin   = xmax - pct,
           high   = sum(pct[idx > mid])) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(group = fct_reorder(group, high), y = as.integer(group),
           text_colour = if_else(abs(idx - mid) == max(abs(idx - mid)), "white", PAL[["ink"]]))
  totals <- distinct(df, group, y, high)
  x_right <- max(df$xmax)

  ggplot(df) +
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = y - 0.33, ymax = y + 0.33, fill = response)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = PAL[["grey"]], linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dotted") +
    geom_text(data = filter(df, pct >= 5),
              aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = y, label = round(pct), colour = text_colour),
              size = 2.7) +
    geom_text(data = totals, aes(x = x_right + 3, y = y, label = sprintf("%.1f%% high", high)),
              hjust = 0, size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", colour = PAL[["accent"]]) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = colorRampPalette(unname(PAL[c("warm", "light", "accent")]))(k)) +
    scale_colour_identity() +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.2))) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = totals$y, labels = totals$group) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_report() +
    theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_blank())
}

fig2 <- plot_likert(sat_likert) +
  labs(title = finding("[Finding about the spread of satisfaction ratings by survey version]"),
       subtitle = "Bars are centred on the midpoint of the scale",
       caption = MOCK_CAPTION)
save_fig(fig2, "fig2_satisfaction_likert", height = 3)
```

# Figure 3. Arrow chart: change from initial to follow-up assessment

Needs: `measure`, `n`, `pre_mean`, `post_mean`, `pre_sd`, `higher_is_better`.
Change is expressed in baseline standard deviations and flipped where lower scores are
better, so an arrow pointing right always means improvement.

```{r fig3-arrows}
plot_change_arrows <- function(df) {
  df <- df |>
    mutate(suppressed = is_suppressed(n, post_mean),
           change = if_else(suppressed, NA_real_,
                            (post_mean - pre_mean) / pre_sd * if_else(higher_is_better, 1, -1)),
           label = sprintf("%.1f to %.1f", pre_mean, post_mean),
           measure = fct_reorder(measure, coalesce(change, -Inf)))
  shown <- filter(df, !suppressed)

  ggplot(df, aes(y = measure)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = PAL[["ink"]], linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_segment(data = shown,
                 aes(x = 0, xend = change, yend = measure, colour = change > 0),
                 linewidth = 1.1, arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.16, "cm"), type = "closed")) +
    geom_text(data = shown,
              aes(x = change, label = label, hjust = if_else(change > 0, -0.15, 1.15)),
              size = 2.6, colour = PAL[["grey"]]) +
    geom_text(data = filter(df, suppressed), aes(x = 0, label = SUPPR_LABEL),
              hjust = -0.2, size = 2.6, fontface = "italic", colour = PAL[["grey"]]) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = PAL[["accent"]], `FALSE` = PAL[["warm"]]),
                        guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.25))) +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = levels(df$measure)) +   # layers use subsets; fix the order
    labs(x = "Change in baseline standard deviations (right = improvement)", y = NULL) +
    theme_report()
}

fig3 <- plot_change_arrows(outcomes) +
  labs(title = finding("[Finding about which measures improved most]"),
       subtitle = "Mean score at initial assessment to most recent follow-up",
       caption = paste(MOCK_CAPTION, "Measures with fewer than", SUPPRESS_N, "pairs are suppressed."))
save_fig(fig3, "fig3_outcome_arrows", height = 4)
```

# Figure 4. Unit dot chart: participants reached

Needs: `category`, `n`.

```{r fig4-dots}
plot_unit_dots <- function(df, unit, rows = 10) {
  df <- mutate(df, category = fct_inorder(category))
  dots <- df |>
    uncount(round(n / unit)) |>
    mutate(id = row_number() - 1, col = id %/% rows, row = rows - id %% rows)
  key <- set_names(sprintf("%s (%s)", df$category, comma(df$n)), df$category)

  ggplot(dots, aes(col, row, colour = category)) +
    geom_point(size = 1.7) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_QUAL[seq_len(nlevels(df$category))], labels = key) +
    coord_equal() +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2, override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
    theme_report() +
    theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.title = element_blank(),
          panel.grid = element_blank())
}

DOT_UNIT <- 100
fig4 <- plot_unit_dots(reach, unit = DOT_UNIT) +
  labs(title = paste("The Workstream reached", comma(sum(reach$n)), "participants"),
       subtitle = paste("Each dot represents", DOT_UNIT, "participants"),
       caption = paste(MOCK_CAPTION, "(Total is real; split by round is not.)"))
save_fig(fig4, "fig4_reach_dots", height = 3.2)
```

# Figure 5. Back-to-back bars: who was served vs. who answered the survey

Needs: `category`, `group` (exactly two levels), `n`, `pct`.

```{r fig5-mirror}
plot_mirror <- function(df) {
  df <- df |>
    group_by(category) |>
    filter(!any(is_suppressed(n, pct))) |>      # drop the pair if either side is suppressed
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(group = fct_inorder(group),
           side = if_else(as.integer(group) == 1, -1, 1),
           category = fct_reorder(category, pct, .fun = max))

  ggplot(df, aes(x = side * pct, y = category, fill = group)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", pct), hjust = if_else(side < 0, 1.15, -0.15)),
              size = 2.7, colour = PAL[["ink"]]) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = unname(PAL[c("grey", "accent")])) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = \(x) paste0(abs(x), "%"), expand = expansion(mult = 0.18)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_report() +
    theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_blank())
}

fig5 <- plot_mirror(representation) +
  labs(title = finding("[Finding about whether survey respondents resemble participants served]"),
       subtitle = "Share of each group by race",
       caption = MOCK_CAPTION)
save_fig(fig5, "fig5_representation_mirror", height = 3.2)
```

# Figure 6. Timeline ticks: how quickly each round's grantees began serving

Needs: `group`, `days` (one row per grantee; days from award to first enrolled participant).
Every round is lined up on the same clock, with a count at a common reference point.
One tick per grantee, so no participant-level dates appear.

```{r fig6-ticks}
plot_timeline_ticks <- function(df, ref_days) {
  df <- mutate(df, group = fct_rev(fct_inorder(group)), y = as.integer(group),
               by_ref = days <= ref_days)
  strips <- df |>
    group_by(group, y) |>
    summarise(k = sum(by_ref), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(xmax = max(df$days))

  ggplot(df) +
    geom_rect(data = strips, aes(xmin = 0, xmax = xmax, ymin = y - 0.22, ymax = y + 0.22),
              fill = "white", colour = PAL[["light"]]) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = days, xend = days, y = y - 0.22, yend = y + 0.22, colour = by_ref),
                 linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = ref_days, colour = PAL[["ink"]], linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_text(data = strips, aes(x = ref_days, y = y + 0.4, label = k),
              size = 2.9, fontface = "bold", colour = PAL[["accent"]]) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = PAL[["accent"]], `FALSE` = PAL[["grey"]]),
                        guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.02)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = strips$y, labels = strips$group,
                       expand = expansion(add = c(0.4, 0.6))) +
    labs(x = "Days since the round's award", y = NULL) +
    theme_report() +
    theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
}

fig6 <- plot_timeline_ticks(grantee_start, REF_DAYS) +
  labs(title = finding("[Finding about how quickly each round's grantees began serving participants]"),
       subtitle = paste("One tick per grantee. Numbers: grantees serving within", REF_DAYS, "days"),
       caption = MOCK_CAPTION)
save_fig(fig6, "fig6_grantee_timeline", height = 3.6)
```

# Figure 7. Heatmap with marginal totals: when and where participants enrolled

Needs three tables with the same `x` and `y` factor levels: cells (`x`, `y`, `n`),
`x` totals (`x`, `n`) and `y` totals (`y`, `n`). Read the totals from the export instead of
summing cells, because suppressed cells are blank.

```{r fig7-heat-margins}
plot_margin_bars <- function(totals, var, flip = FALSE) {
  p <- ggplot(totals, aes(x = {{ var }}, y = n, fill = n)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.85) +
    geom_text(data = slice_max(totals, n, n = 1), aes(label = comma(n)),
              size = 2.5, colour = PAL[["accent"]],
              vjust = if (flip) 0.5 else -0.4, hjust = if (flip) 1.15 else 0.5) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = PAL[["light"]], high = PAL[["accent"]], guide = "none") +
    theme_void()
  if (flip) {
    p + coord_flip() + scale_y_reverse(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.5, 0)))
  } else {
    p + scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2)))
  }
}

plot_heat_margins <- function(cells, x_totals, y_totals) {
  y_levels <- rev(levels(cells$y))                 # first level at the top
  relevel_y <- \(df) mutate(df, y = factor(y, levels = y_levels))
  heat <- ggplot(relevel_y(cells), aes(x, y, fill = n)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, is.na(n)), colour = PAL[["grey"]], size = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = PAL[["light"]], high = PAL[["accent"]], na.value = "white",
                        labels = comma, name = NULL) +
    scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(check.overlap = TRUE)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_report() +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.justification = "right", legend.key.height = unit(0.25, "cm"),
          legend.key.width = unit(1, "cm"))

  plot_spacer() + plot_margin_bars(x_totals, x) +
    plot_margin_bars(relevel_y(y_totals), y, flip = TRUE) + heat +
    plot_layout(widths = c(1, 4), heights = c(1, 3)) &
    theme(plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2))
}

fig7 <- plot_heat_margins(enroll_cells, enroll_x_totals, enroll_y_totals) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = finding("[Finding about when and where enrollment was concentrated]"),
    subtitle = "Participants enrolled by quarter and region; bars show totals",
    caption = paste(MOCK_CAPTION, "Dotted cells are fewer than", SUPPRESS_N, "participants."),
    theme = theme_report())
save_fig(fig7, "fig7_enrollment_heatmap", height = 4.6)
```

# Figure 8. Dot strips: how much satisfaction varies between providers

Needs: `item`, `provider`, `n`, `pct` (one row per provider per survey item).
Each dot is a provider and is not labelled; the tick is the respondent-weighted rate.

```{r fig8-strips}
plot_provider_strips <- function(df) {
  df <- df |>
    filter(!is_suppressed(n, pct)) |>
    group_by(item) |>
    mutate(item_pct = weighted.mean(pct, n)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(item = fct_reorder(item, item_pct))

  ggplot(df, aes(y = item)) +
    geom_point(aes(x = pct, colour = pct), size = 1.1, alpha = 0.75,
               position = position_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.28, seed = 1)) +
    geom_point(data = distinct(df, item, item_pct), aes(x = item_pct),
               shape = "|", size = 6, colour = PAL[["ink"]]) +
    scale_colour_gradient2(low = PAL[["warm"]], mid = PAL[["grey"]], high = PAL[["accent"]],
                           midpoint = weighted.mean(df$pct, df$n), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(scale = 1)) +
    labs(x = "Agree or strongly agree", y = NULL) +
    theme_report() +
    theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = PAL[["light"]]))
}

fig8 <- plot_provider_strips(provider_items) +
  labs(title = finding("[Finding about how widely providers differ on each survey item]"),
       subtitle = "Each dot is one provider; the tick is the rate across all respondents",
       caption = paste(MOCK_CAPTION, "Providers with fewer than", SUPPRESS_N, "surveys not shown."))
save_fig(fig8, "fig8_provider_strips", height = 4)
```

# Figure 9. Ranked dots with component ticks

Needs: an overall table (`row`, `n`, `pct`) and a parts table (`row`, `part`, `n`, `pct`).

```{r fig9-ranked}
plot_ranked_parts <- function(overall, parts) {
  overall <- overall |>
    filter(!is_suppressed(n, pct)) |>
    arrange(desc(pct)) |>
    mutate(row_label = fct_rev(fct_inorder(sprintf("%2d  %s", row_number(), row))))
  parts <- parts |>
    filter(!is_suppressed(n, pct)) |>
    inner_join(select(overall, row, row_label), by = "row") |>
    mutate(part = fct_inorder(part))
  ranges <- parts |>
    group_by(row_label) |>
    summarise(lo = min(pct), hi = max(pct))

  ggplot(mapping = aes(y = row_label)) +
    geom_segment(data = ranges, aes(x = lo, xend = hi, yend = row_label),
                 colour = PAL[["light"]], linewidth = 3) +
    geom_point(data = parts, aes(x = pct, colour = part), shape = "|", size = 4.5) +
    geom_point(data = overall, aes(x = pct), colour = PAL[["ink"]], size = 2.4) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = PAL_QUAL[seq_len(nlevels(parts$part))]) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(scale = 1)) +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = levels(overall$row_label)) +
    labs(x = "Reported high satisfaction", y = NULL) +
    theme_report() +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 0))
}

fig9 <- plot_ranked_parts(region_overall, region_parts) +
  labs(title = finding("[Finding about how regions rank and how far survey versions spread within each]"),
       subtitle = "Dot: all respondents. Ticks: each survey version",
       caption = paste(MOCK_CAPTION, "Groups under", SUPPRESS_N, "not shown."))
save_fig(fig9, "fig9_region_ranked", height = 4)
```

# Figure 10. Small-multiple scatter: provider size and satisfaction

Needs: `provider`, `group`, `n`, `pct` (one row per provider).

```{r fig10-scatter}
plot_provider_scatter <- function(df) {
  df <- df |>
    filter(!is_suppressed(n, pct)) |>
    mutate(group = fct_inorder(group) |> fct_relevel(sort))

  ggplot(df, aes(n, pct)) +
    geom_point(colour = PAL[["accent"]], alpha = 0.55, size = 1.4) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE,
                colour = PAL[["warm"]], linewidth = 0.7) +
    facet_wrap(vars(group), nrow = 1) +
    scale_x_log10(labels = comma, breaks = breaks_log(3)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(scale = 1)) +
    labs(x = "Surveys completed (log scale)", y = "Reported high satisfaction") +
    theme_report() +
    theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = PAL[["light"]]),
          panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
}

fig10 <- plot_provider_scatter(providers) +
  labs(title = finding("[Finding about whether larger providers report higher satisfaction]"),
       subtitle = "Each dot is one provider",
       caption = paste(MOCK_CAPTION, "Providers with fewer than", SUPPRESS_N, "surveys not shown."))
save_fig(fig10, "fig10_provider_scatter", height = 3)
```
